itemList.description: Routine and General maintenance of truck mount Hydraulic Boom lift (Sky Lift) (Excluding major breakdown) Operation of boom lift (sky lift) safety as per recommended practice including that of truck. Checking and top up if required hydraulic fluid level. Checking any oil/ fluid leakage and rectify. Check and top-up water/ coolant in radiator. Check for any leaks in radiator and rectify if required. Check for normal working of all electrical/ electronic devices, instruments panel meters and rectify if found faulty. Clean air filter and refixing it. Check and top-up broke fluid of required. Check wheel nuts. If found loose broke tighten them. Check and adjust / rectify parking broke and foot brake. Check for fan belt tension if found sagging tighten it. Check fuel filter. I sediments are found drain our and remove. Oil levels in transmission and hydraulic systems, axle, actuators are to be monitored and top-up regularly. Propeller shaft, steer axle all pivot pins and all relevant parts/ sub-systems are to be greased regularly as per recommended practice by OEM. Inspect / check electrical wiring and repair / insulate if required. Inspect, check and clean battery terminals and wash and replace if required corroded terminals. Along with routine maintenance the engaged staff must involve in regular maintenance works of streetlights and any other miscellaneous works. Vehicle should be kept neat and clean by washing the vehicle at least twice in a month. Driver, Cleaner and Operators scope of work : Eligibility Criteria: driver should hold a Heavy Vehicle Driving Licence Issued from the RTO Karnataka and all the engaged staff including driver should be available to the service 24x7 including government holidays. in case regular staff is not available alternate arrangements should be made. Role and Responsibilities: A hydraulic lift vehicle drivers, cleaner and operators are responsible for safely operating, manoeuvring, and maintaining machinery with hydraulic lifting systems. A hydraulic boom lift driver is responsible for safely transporting maintenance crews to elevated heights, manoeuvring the platform around street obstacles, and operating base-level or basket controls to facilitate efficient streetlight repairs while strictly adhering to high-risk safety protocols. Pre-Operation & Equipment Maintenance :Daily Inspections: Conduct routine walk-around inspections (fluid levels, tires, wire ropes, and outriggers) before driving or lifting to ensure safe working conditions Hydraulic Checks: Inspect hydraulic hoses and cylinders for leaks or pressure drops Safety Tests: Test emergency stop switches, dead-man pedals (enable switches), and the auxiliary lowering system daily to guarantee ground descent in case of power failure Defect Reporting: Immediately report any mechanical, structural, or electrical defects and red tag to the maintenance contractor. Site Setup & Positioning: Safe Ground Assessment: Ensure the vehicle is parked on firm, level ground, avoiding steep inclines (typically anything over 5 to 10 depending on the manufacturer) or soft soil. Traffic & Pedestrian Control: Set up traffic cones, warning signs, and safety barricades to secure the work zone and protect both the crew and the public. Stabilizer Deployment: Fully deploy, level, and secure outriggers or stabilizers before elevating the boom. Clearance Check: Ensure the boom swing radius is free from overhead obstructions like tree branches, power cables, and moving traffic. Safe Operation at Heights: Basket Manoeuvrability: Accurately manipulate joysticks to elevate, telescope, and rotate the platform so the technician can easily access the luminaire, wiring, or bulbs. PPE & Harness Compliance: Wear and enforce the mandatory use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment, including hard hats, safety vests, and most importantly, a properly secured safety harness tied directly to the basket's anchor point.
